title: Strain-driven orbital-selective reconstruction and bicollinear-to-stripe evolution in FeTe
authors: Zhenfeng Ouyang, Yin Chen, Yi-Heng Tian, Jia-Ming Wang, Rong-Qiang He, Kai Liu, Zhong-Yi Lu
abstract: FeTe, as a representative parent material among iron-based superconductors, provides an ideal platform for exploring the interplay among orbital-selective correlations, magnetism, and unconventional superconductivity. However, a unified picture of the correlated electronic structure and magnetism of FeTe under strain remains to be fully clarified. Here, combining density functional theory plus dynamical mean-field theory and Heisenberg model analysis, we uncover an orbital-selective reconstruction of the correlated electronic structure and reveal a strain-driven trajectory from bicollinear to stripe antiferromagnetism (AFM) via an intermediate competing staggered $n$-mer AFM regime in FeTe. Moderate strain gives rise to a regime where more coherent quasiparticles coexist with suppressed local moments. Further strain drives FeTe into an incoherent correlated regime with robust local moments and Fe-$3d_{z^2}$-dominated low-energy states. These results establish a strain-driven trajectory across distinct magnetic and correlated electronic states in FeTe.
summary: This theoretical study investigates how applying tensile strain tunes the electronic and magnetic properties of the iron-based superconductor FeTe. Using DFT+DMFT and Heisenberg models, the authors reveal a strain-driven pathway that causes the magnetic order to evolve from bicollinear to stripe antiferromagnetism. This magnetic change is intrinsically linked to an orbital-selective reconstruction of the electronic structure, providing a unified picture of correlated behavior.
main_problem: To establish a complete, unified, strain-driven trajectory connecting the magnetic and correlated electronic states of FeTe, specifically addressing the orbital-selective reconstruction and the evolution from bicollinear to stripe antiferromagnetism (AFM).
main_result: Tensile strain drives a pronounced orbital-selective reconstruction and a magnetic transition trajectory from bicollinear to stripe AFM via an intermediate staggered n-mer AFM regime.
method: The study combines Density Functional Theory plus Dynamical Mean-Field Theory (DFT+DMFT) calculations with Heisenberg model analysis.
model_or_system: The system is FeTe, a parent material among iron-based superconductors, studied under systematically varied in-plane biaxial tensile strain.
key_observables: Momentum-resolved spectral functions, imaginary part of the Matsubara self-energy, local spin susceptibility, and local spin moment ($M_z$).
important_parameters: Tensile strain (ranging from small to large values), and the magnetic coupling parameters ($J_1, J_2, J_3$) derived from the Heisenberg model.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on DFT+DMFT to capture correlated electronic structure effects and an effective Heisenberg model to map the magnetic phase transitions.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the spectral evolution under strain, showing changes in coherence and spectral weight, alongside plots detailing the evolution of magnetic susceptibilities and local spin moments across different strain regimes.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the effect of tensile strain on FeTe, first using DFT+DMFT to track orbital reconstruction and correlation strength, and then coupling these electronic findings to the magnetic phase diagram derived from Heisenberg model analysis, establishing the full strain-driven trajectory.
why_interesting: The study provides a detailed, quantitative mapping of how external strain tunes the interplay between electronic correlations (orbital selectivity) and magnetic order in a strongly correlated material, which is a key theme in modern condensed matter theory.
